key_insight: PANY shows that 6D pose estimation for unseen objects can be done without CAD models by using arbitrary reference images, not just a single paired anchor. This makes pose recovery more robust to occlusion, viewpoint changes, and low overlap between query and reference views.
problem_solved: The paper addresses open-world 6D object pose estimation when objects are unseen and no CAD model is available. Existing model-free methods often struggle with occlusion and large viewpoint changes because they rely on limited single-anchor matching.
method: Introduces PANY, a unified model-free framework for pose estimation from arbitrary references.
Supports both RGB and RGB-D inputs, enabling flexible use across different sensing setups.
Designed to improve robustness under low query-reference overlap, occlusion, and wide viewpoint variation.
impact: This matters for robotics and embodied AI because it reduces dependence on object-specific CAD assets and costly onboarding. Practitioners can estimate poses more flexibly in real-world, open-world environments where reference views are imperfect.
visual_elements: A before-vs-after comparison of model-based, single-anchor model-free, and arbitrary-reference pose estimation
A pipeline diagram showing query image, arbitrary reference(s), and pose output
An occlusion and viewpoint-change illustration highlighting robustness
Icons for RGB and RGB-D inputs to show modality support
paper_title: Pose Anything Anywhere:Model-free Object Poses from Arbitrary References
paper_authors: Hongli Xu, Jiaqi Hu, Junwen Huang, Boyang Zhong, Peter KT Yu
